 1                         MEMORANDUM OF POINTS AND AUTHORITIES

 2     I.    INTRODUCTION

 3           This case arises from Capital One’s pervasive and undisclosed practice of collecting and

 4 transmitting its customers’ sensitive personal and financial information to third parties through an

 5 extensive web-tracking ecosystem secretly embedded in its online properties. From the start, Plaintiffs

 6 have alleged that Capital One knowingly configured its website and backend systems to transmit

 7 identifying and financial data—without consent—to third parties for Capital One’s own commercial

 8 benefit. Plaintiffs also alleged those third parties allowed fourth parties to use and benefit from

 9 Plaintiffs’ personal and financial information.
10           Discovery proceeded accordingly. Plaintiffs sought evidence on the full range of technologies
11 Capital One used to disclose customer data, including both browser-based trackers and server-to-

12 server technologies. The Complaint expressly contemplated these disclosures from the wide panoply

13 of technologies that Capital One uses, and Plaintiffs’ discovery requests tracked that broad scope—

14 seeking to identify what data was shared, with whom, through which technologies, and over what

15 period of time.

16           Capital One nevertheless chose obstruction over disclosure. Throughout discovery, it engaged
17 in a pattern of selective production and delay—providing partial information, denying relevance, and

18 withholding documents and testimony concerning server-to-server technologies that went to the heart

19 of Plaintiffs’ claims. It repeatedly represented that its responses were complete, even as it resisted

20 producing scores of documents concerning its use of server-to-server technologies. Only after months

21 of meet-and-confer efforts, when it faced imminent depositions, and repeated court involvement did

22 Capital One begin to acknowledge—often mere hours before a critical deposition—that it had, in fact,

23 also used server-to-server technologies to transmit Plaintiffs’ data to third parties.

24           Even after those disclosures, it turns out that Capital One’s production is still incomplete.
25 After fact discovery closed, after Plaintiffs served their expert reports, and only because this Court

26 compelled a deposition on server-to-server technology, Capital One produced additional documents

27 and partial supplemental responses, disclosing, for the first time in this litigation, that it uses two other

28 server-to-server technologies to transmit Plaintiffs’ and the putative class’s data, Skai FTP and Google
